messages:
elena: Quick note from the v4-quant onboarding run — we get solid perf/cost wins but a small regression on the 'multi-step reasoning' slice (multi-turn chains > 6 turns).
jordy: saw that. numbers?
elena: delta_mrr = -0.021, p=0.028, n=2700; secondary metric (answer_f1) delta = -0.009, p=0.14. latency down 24% p50, cost/token -28%.
micah: so classic economics vs fidelity tradeoff. Our current promote gate is binary: any critical slice mrr<-0.02 & p<0.05 => hard_autofallback. That would block this.
elena: given the clear infra wins, can we introduce a weighted gate that factors in latency and cost improvements before auto-fallback? I don't want to bypass safety, but for borderline regressions there should be a path.
jordy: proposal: add an "econ_adjustment" multiplier that relaxes the mrr threshold proportionally to normalized latency+cost improvements up to a cap. e.g., if latency_improve >=20% and cost>=20% then allow mrr loss up to 0.03 with replicate-run requirement.
micah: careful: mixing scales is tricky. Also we need deterministic, auditable rules — avoid ad-hoc approvals. Could implement as a two-path gate: 1) Normal path (hard_autofallback) 2) Economics-exception path -> requires replicate-run + manual signoff by release lead.
elena: that matches my comfort level. For this run prefer "economics-exception" behavior.
eval-bot: Eval summary: slice=multi-step(>6 turns); n=2698; delta_mrr=-0.0208; p_mrr=0.028; CI=[-0.035,-0.007]; delta_f1=-0.009; p_f1=0.146; latency_p50_improve=24%; cost_token_improve=28%. Link: https://console.redwood/testing/runs/2026-03-04/1839991234\jordy: config snippet suggestion:
```
"rollout_gates": {
  "slices": ["multi-step","long-doc"],
  "economics_exception": {
    "enabled": true,
    "min_latency_improve_pct": 15,
    "min_cost_improve_pct": 15,
    "max_mrr_loss_allowed": 0.03,
    "action_on_trigger": "replicate_then_manual",
    "replicate_params": {"duration_hours":2, "seed_lock": true}
  }
}
```\micah: add requirement: economics_exception only applies if secondary metrics (F1/EM) delta > -0.02 or p>0.1 — this avoids accepting catastrophic failures that MRR misses.\eljena: small typo (micah) — I'm elena ;). I like that extra safeguard. Also require min_unique_sessions for the slice (>=800) to avoid small-N noise. Current n=2698 so OK.\jordy: ops-bot, can you create a replicate run with the same seed (offline replay) and tag it econ-exception?\ops-bot: Replicate job scheduled: job=replica-1839991234-01; offline-replay seeded; min_unique_sessions=900; duration=2h. Will post results when finished.\micah: action items: (1) add econ-exception path to rollout-config (2) require replicate_then_manual for exceptions (3) patch runbook with decision matrix and audit log fields.
elena: I'll draft the PR and include the eval link + runbook blurb. Jordy, micah, please review.
jordy: LGTM provisional. We'll prefer replicate outcomes before any manual signoff.
micah: noted. If replicate confirms mrr delta p<0.05, we block promote and require rollback in next canary promotion. If not reproducible, allow promote but flag for 24h watch.
elena: thanks all — scheduling a follow-up once replicate job completes. :thumbsup:
